meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/03, Wednesday 14 June 2023), downloaded from www.ocr.org.uk. Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: 52 markers summing to exactly the printed 100, the only check OCR allows. Coded WITH mark_split, derived from OCR's part totals and partial-credit routes.

coding_notes: q1a tagged properties_of_3d_solids and q1b/q1c properties_of_2d_shapes — (a) picks the non-prism from four solids, (b) names a triangle by two properties at once, and (c) draws a quadrilateral meeting a symmetry condition and an angle condition.
q10c (more machines, fewer days) tagged inverse_proportion: the mark scheme's route is 3 × 25 ÷ 15, which only works because the relationship is inverse.

q13a and q13b are about the square root symbol returning only the positive root — tagged indices, the documented handling for roots. (b) asks what changes if the letter need not be positive, and the mark scheme's answer is that nothing does.
q15 (criticise a bar chart whose age groups overlap) tagged grouped_frequency_tables rather than simple_charts: the fault is in the class intervals, not the drawing.
q17b tagged upper_and_lower_bounds — two error intervals from different roundings, compared to show an overlap.
q19a and q19b tagged relative_frequency: both scale a sample proportion, and (c) is the sample-size argument for why the larger one is better.
q22 tagged constructions then loci: two of the five marks are the perpendicular bisector's arcs, two the angle bisector's, and the last is the point where the loci meet.
